title: BitLocker asks for recovery key
symptom: Laptop asks for a BitLocker recovery key after a BIOS update
user_description: My laptop installed an update last night and now it's a blue screen asking for a BitLocker recovery key. I never got any key! Is my laptop broken?

options.text: Reinstall Windows to get past the screen
options.why: This wipes the drive and all his data. The key exists and can be found.

options.text: Verify who he is, then give him the 48-digit recovery key from where the company stores it (such as Active Directory, Entra ID or Intune)
options.why: Firmware updates can trigger BitLocker recovery. Company devices normally back up their key, and verifying identity first stops someone else getting into the laptop.

options.text: Tell him to keep restarting until it stops asking
options.why: The screen will keep coming back. It needs the recovery key.

options.text: Try some likely passwords as the key
options.why: The recovery key is a 48-digit number, not a password, so guessing will not work.

hints: Where do company devices usually keep their BitLocker key?
Why must you check who is asking before giving the key?
What could stop this happening next time?
real_world_tip: Before future BIOS or firmware updates, suspend BitLocker so the update does not trigger the recovery screen. It turns back on after the restart.
